the-lives-of-the-twelve-caesars-volume-0: Before there were emperors, there was Julius Caesar — the general who crossed the Rubicon and ended the Roman Republic. Suetonius traces his rise from ambitious young politician to dictator, ending with the daggers of the Ides of March. Packed with anecdotes about his charm, ambition, and famous last words, it is the ancient biography behind the legend.
two-months-in-the-camp-of-big-bear: Theresa Gowanlock and Theresa Delaney were taken captive during the North-West Rebellion of 1885, when Big Bear's Cree band seized them in the Frog Lake tragedy. This memoir recounts their two months as prisoners — the fear, the forced marches, and the small kindnesses that kept them alive. A rare firsthand account of one of the Canadian West's darkest episodes.
young-knights-of-the-empire-their-code-a: Lord Baden-Powell, the founder of Scouting, offers more yarns and teachings for his young knights of the empire. The scout code — honor, loyalty, and service — is illustrated through stirring stories of adventure and daring. Written by the Chief Scout himself, the book captures the movement's spirit in its heroic early years.
why-we-are-at-war: President Woodrow Wilson's historic war message of April 1917 asked Congress to take America into the Great War — to make the world safe for democracy. These pages preserve the speech and its context. A landmark of American oratory and a fateful moment in world history.
a-short-history-of-the-great-war: A. F. Pollard condenses the Great War into a short, clear history — its causes, campaigns, and consequences. Written while memories were fresh, it served a generation seeking to understand. A solid first account of the catastrophe. Maps, battles, and home-front trials are set forth in admirable brevity.
an-art-lovers-guide-to-the-exposition-ex: Sheldon Cheney guides art lovers through the great San Francisco exposition — its architecture, sculpture, and mural paintings clearly explained. His expert eye makes the fair's vanished beauty live again. An invaluable companion to a lost wonderland. His clear prose makes the fair's glories plain to every reader.
springhaven-a-tale-of-the-great-war: R. D. Blackmore's Springhaven — his last novel — tells of England's great war against Napoleon, with smugglers, sailors, and village folk caught in vast events. The Lorna Doone author's farewell to fiction is gallant and tender. A fine final tale from a beloved writer.
